brief: 069 the Fixer redone (Sky, 2026-10-27: 'Go'): Sky's final concept fixer_v7_cutout (intake pose) -> Tripo 3.1 -> the hybrid fit -> the static check. No animation until Sky's OK.
note: Sky's 'Go' 2026-10-27; then Sky: 'Player Models should be created at 30k triangles' (the cell: Scout, Fixer, Tech, Enforcer). Pass mesh (20k, $0.60) kept for comparison; pass mesh30k: one take at about $0.60, budget $1.00, a retry only for a call that fails at $0

model.note: Sky's pick for 3D (memory: Tripo 3.1, ~$0.60 via Runware). Runware's Tripo 3.1 page (https://runware.ai/docs/models/tripo-v3-1): inputs.images takes 1 to 4 images for multiview-to-3D, order not stated there; Tripo's own API orders multi-view as [front, left, back, right] with views omittable (front required, at least 2: https://developers.tripo3d.com/en/docs/generation-multiview-to-model/standard), so the three real views go in that order and no right view is invented. faceLimit by the person's kind (faceLimitByKind; the cell at 30000). Runware's page lists 20000 as Tripo's maximum, but the October Fixer was made at 30000 through Runware (28,428 triangles); the first v7 take used 20000 and returned 18,841. pbr off: the game's figures are matte. orientation default: the fit normalises facing itself.

faceLimitByKind.note: Sky, 2026-10-27: 'Player Models should be created at 30k triangles'. A person row's kind picks its face limit; the October Fixer was made through Runware with tripo:v3.1@0 faceLimit 30000 (tools/figures/fixer_gen.py, 28,428 triangles), so Runware's documented 20000 maximum is not enforced.

people.label: the Fixer, Sky's final concept v7: ivory and aubergine, long asymmetric wrap skirt to mid-calf split at her left hip, open back, sleeves joined by a band over each shoulder with pointed cut-outs, top knot and ponytail, block-heel ankle boots

looseRulesNote: none: the ponytail and the long skirt take nearest-body weights for now (Aster, 2026-10-27); their extra bones are a later hero step

hat.note: as e2e.json hairRule false: a person's own cap was generated with their own hair and already fits it; the hair-under-hat rule is for a hat moved onto another head (the G path). Applied here it pulled the guard's fringe under the brim into spikes, which the LOD0 reduction opened into dark cracks (2026-10-27).

rest.note: as e2e.json: the rest is the intake A-pose she was generated in; the Humanoid T reference with neutral legs is <id>_H_avatarT.fbx

lod0.note: as e2e.json: LOD0 is the generated mesh at full detail
